Prepared Food and Beverage Solutions.heading: Prepared Food and Beverage Solutions
Prepared Food and Beverage Solutions.text:
Prepared Food and Beverage Solutions segment revenue was flat for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to the same period in 2025, including an $8 million benefit from favorable foreign currency translation. Organic revenue declined during the period, primarily driven by lower equipment volumes across certain end markets within the segment.

Prepared Food and Beverage Solutions segment Adjusted EBITDA was $90 million, or 17.5%, of segment revenue, for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $94 million, or 18.2% of segment revenue, for the same period in 2025. These factors were partially offset by a favorable net tariff impact. Adjusted EBITDA margin decreased 70 bps from the prior-year period.

Protein Solutions segment Adjusted EBITDA was $112 million or 24.0% of segment revenue, for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $86 million, or 20.5% of segment revenue, for the same period in 2025. The increase of $26 million, or 30.2%, was primarily driven by higher gross margin resulting from increased volume, synergy realization and a favorable net tariff impact, partially offset by higher inflationary costs. Adjusted EBITDA margin increased 350 bps from the prior-year period.

sga.text: Selling, general and administrative expense decreased $5 million compared to the same period in the prior year. As a percentage of revenue, selling, general and administrative expense decreased 30 bps to 25.5% compared to 25.8%, primarily due to the alignment of certain expenses between cost of sales and selling, general and administrative expense discussed above, partially offset by higher integration-related costs and acquired intangible asset amortization resulting from third-quarter 2025 measurement-period valuation adjustments.

da_op.text: • Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin: We define Adjusted EBITDA as earnings before income taxes, interest expense (income), net, other financing income, pension expense other than service cost, restructuring costs, M&A related costs, including acquisition and integration-related expenses, one-time impairment charges, and depreciation and amortization, including acquisition-related depreciation and amortization. We define Adjusted EBITDA margin as Adjusted EBITDA divided by revenue.

nonop.heading: Interest expense, net
nonop.text: Interest expense, net, decreased by $8 million compared to the prior-year period, driven by lower outstanding debt balances, a more favorable debt mix and benefits from the Company’s net investment hedges during the third quarter of 2026.

tax.text: The effective tax rate for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was 20.5%, compared to 20.4% for the same period in 2025. The 2026 tax rate reflected a favorable discrete tax benefit of $2 million primarily related to the finalization of prior-year tax return positions.

net.heading: Net income and Adjusted EBITDA
net.text:
Net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $70 million compared with $66 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of $4 million. Net income margin increased to 7.0%, from 6.7% in the prior-year period, primarily due to lower interest expense and selling, general and administrative expense, partially offset by lower gross profit margin.

Adjusted EBITDA was $179 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared with $171 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of $8 million. Adjusted EBITDA margin increased 90 bps to 18.0% compared to 17.1% in the prior-year period. The increase was primarily driven by a favorable mix of recurring revenue relative to non-recurring revenue, cost synergy realization, favorable pricing and lower operating expenses, which more than offset lower volume leverage.

ocf.text: • Free cash flow: We define free cash flow as cash provided by operating activities, less capital expenditures, plus proceeds from sale of fixed assets and pension contributions.

da.text: • Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin: We define Adjusted EBITDA as earnings before income taxes, interest expense (income), net, other financing income, pension expense other than service cost, restructuring costs, M&A related costs, including acquisition and integration-related expenses, one-time impairment charges, and depreciation and amortization, including acquisition-related depreciation and amortization. We define Adjusted EBITDA margin as Adjusted EBITDA divided by revenue.

wc.text: Additionally, the cash flows generated by our operations are expected to be sufficient to satisfy our principal cash requirements that include our working capital needs, new product development, restructuring expenses, capital expenditures, income taxes, debt interest and repayments, dividends, share repurchases and other financing arrangements.

fcf.text: • Free cash flow: We define free cash flow as cash provided by operating activities, less capital expenditures, plus proceeds from sale of fixed assets and pension contributions.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text: Total revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 decreased $7 million, or 0.7%, compared with the same period in 2025 as volume declines in the Prepared Food and Beverage Solutions segment offset volume growth in Protein Solutions. Foreign currency translation did not have a significant impact on the year-over-year change in revenue.

Prepared Food and Beverage Solutions.heading: Prepared Food and Beverage Solutions
Prepared Food and Beverage Solutions.text:
Prepared Food and Beverage Solutions segment revenue decreased by $35 million, or 6.3%, during the three months ended September 30, 2026. Organic revenue declined primarily due to lower volumes across certain end markets within the segment’s Diversified Food and Health business. Foreign currency translation did not have a significant impact on the year-over-year change in segment revenue.

Prepared Food and Beverage Solutions segment Adjusted EBITDA was $101 million, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease of $1 million, or 1.0%, compared with the prior-year period. Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin increased 90 bps to 19.2%, as benefits from restructuring actions within the segment’s warehouse automation business, favorable segment mix, cost synergy realization and favorable pricing more than offset lower volume leverage.

Protein Solutions.heading: Protein Solutions
Protein Solutions.text:
Protein Solutions segment revenue increased by $28 million, or 6.3% during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with the same period in 2025.Organic revenue increased primarily due to higher volumes across end markets within the Poultry business. Foreign currency translation did not have a significant impact on the year-over-year change in segment revenue.

Protein Solutions segment Adjusted EBITDA was $105 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $11 million, or 11.7%, compared with the prior-year period. Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin increas ed 110 bps to 22.4% , primarily due to higher volumes and synergy realization.

intro.text: We are a leading and diversified global technology solutions and service provider to high-value segments of the food and beverage industry. We design, produce, and service sophisticated products and systems for multi-national and regional customers. Our purpose is to transform the future of food by providing solutions that substantially enhance our customers’ success, and in doing so design, produce and service sophisticated and critical products and systems for food and beverage companies that increase yields, boost efficiency, and improve food safety.

gp.heading: Gross Profit and Gross Profit Margin
gp.text: Gross profit margin increased 130 bps to 36.5% compared to 35.2% in 2023. The increase was driven primarily by higher volume and pricing as well as savings from our 2022/2023 restructuring plan and sourcing initiatives. This was partially offset by input cost inflation and a stronger mix of non-recurring revenue compared to the prior year, which tends to have lower margins than recurring revenue.

rd.text: Beginning in 2022, the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 eliminated the option to deduct research and development expenditures immediately in the year incurred and requires taxpayers to amortize such expenditures in the U.S. over five years. As a result, we experienced an adverse impact to our cash from continuing operations of $11 million in 2024 and will experience approximately a $7 million decrease in cash from continuing operations in 2025. The impact will continue over the five-year amortization period but decrease each year.

ga.heading: Selling, general and administrative expense
ga.text: Selling, general and administrative expense increased $97.1 million compared to the prior year, and as a percent of revenue increased 490 bps to 29.5% compared to 24.6% in 2023. This increase was primarily due to higher M&A related cost in the amount of $79.9 million incurred in connection with the Marel Transaction, higher compensation expense from the long term incentive plan as well as merit increases, and higher marketing expenses. The increase was partially offset by savings from our restructuring program.

sga.heading: Selling, general and administrative expense
sga.text: Selling, general and administrative expense increased $97.1 million compared to the prior year, and as a percent of revenue increased 490 bps to 29.5% compared to 24.6% in 2023. This increase was primarily due to higher M&A related cost in the amount of $79.9 million incurred in connection with the Marel Transaction, higher compensation expense from the long term incentive plan as well as merit increases, and higher marketing expenses. The increase was partially offset by savings from our restructuring program.

nonop.heading: Interest expense
nonop.text: Interest expense decreased $4.9 million compared to 2023. This decrease was due to the Company having a lower average debt balance and lower weighted average interest rate, including the impacts of the interest rate swaps, during 2024 compared to 2023.

tax.text: For the year ended December 31, 2024, we recognized income from discontinued operations, net of income taxes, of $0.8 million. For the year ended December 31, 2023, we recognized income from discontinued operations, net of income taxes, of $453.3 million, which included the gain on the sale of AeroTech of $443.7 million, net of tax, that was completed during the third quarter of 2023.

For free cash flow purposes, we consider contributions to pension plans to be more comparable to the payment of debt, and therefore exclude these contributions from the calculation of free cash flow.

wc.text: Additionally, the cash flows generated by the continuing operations of the combined company are expected to be sufficient to satisfy our principal cash requirements that include our working capital needs, new product development, restructuring expenses, capital expenditures, income taxes, debt interest and repayments, dividends, and other financing arrangements.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text: Total revenue in 2024 increased $51.6 million or 3.1% compared to 2023. Organic revenue grew by $59.4 million and foreign currency translation was unfavorable by $7.8 million compared to the prior year. The increase in organic revenue was primarily the result of higher pricing as well as an increase in volume for non-recurring revenue. Recurring revenue was flat year over year.

gp.heading: Gross profit margin
gp.text: Gross profit margin decreased 140 bps to 35.1% compared to 36.5% in 2024. The decrease was driven primarily by tariff impacts and operating inefficiencies on select projects within our Prepared Food and Beverage Solutions segment. This decrease was partially offset by synergy savings and an increased mix of recurring revenue compared to the prior year, which tends to have higher margins than non-recurring revenue.

ga.heading: Selling, general and administrative expense
ga.text: Selling, general and administrative expense increased $609.2 million compared to the prior year. This increase was primarily driven by the acquisition of Marel and higher costs associated with the integration. Selling, general and administrative expense as a percentage of revenue was flat compared to 2024.

sga.heading: Selling, general and administrative expense
sga.text: Selling, general and administrative expense increased $609.2 million compared to the prior year. This increase was primarily driven by the acquisition of Marel and higher costs associated with the integration. Selling, general and administrative expense as a percentage of revenue was flat compared to 2024.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text: Total revenue in 2025 increased $2,082.2 million or 121.3% compared to 2024. The acquisition of Marel provided additional revenue of $1,966.0 million, which is inclusive of a favorable foreign currency translation impact of $50.5 million. Organic revenue grew by $39.8 million and foreign currency translation was favorable by $76.5 million compared to the prior year. The increase in organic revenue was primarily the result of an increase in volume for recurring revenue.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Cash and equivalents
accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: Recurring revenue accounted for 50% of total revenue in 2025.
No single customer accounted for more than 10% of our total revenue in any of the last three fiscal years.
International sales accounted for 62% of our 2025 revenue.
During 2025, our foreign subsidiaries generated 62% of our revenue.

Marel’s total assets and total revenues excluded from our assessment represented approximately 17% and 53% of the Company’s consolidated total assets and consolidated total revenues, respectively, as of and for the year ended December 31, 2025.
We do not use single source suppliers for the majority of our raw material purchases and believe the available supplies of raw materials are adequate to meet our needs.
Our performance also depends on our ability to retain and motivate our officers and key employees.
We rely on our ability to successfully grow our installed base through long-term customer relationships.
We depend on our ability to successfully grow our installed base through long-term customer relationships.

Continuing demand for such equipment, systems, software and services depends on our ability to successfully deliver solutions based on customers’ needs and execute the initial installation in a timely and professional manner that encourages the customer to continue transacting with us in the future.
Because our customers rely on high throughput requirements and deal with highly perishable goods, our ability to deliver prompt and timely service is essential to our aftermarket business.
Our business operations rely upon secure information technology systems for data capture, processing, storage, and reporting.
Our exposure will depend on many factors but, generally, an increase in our exposure will be correlated to an increase in the market price and in the volatility of our common stock.
Our ability to make scheduled payments on or to refinance our debt obligations will depend on our financial and operating performance.
These payments typically rely upon the usage of the underlying asset.
